Privacy Policy

Effective 22 September 2026

Note Builder is published by Essential Software. This policy describes what data the app stores, where it lives, and what leaves your device.

On-device storage

All pages, drafts, images, favourites, preferences, and UI state are stored locally on your device. If you sign in with Google, your notes are additionally backed up to Essential Software's servers — see below.

Google sign-in & sync

Signing in is optional. It's handled by Google — Essential Software never sees your Google password. Essential Software receives your Google account identifier and email address, and stores them along with a session token so you stay signed in. While signed in, your notes (including embedded images) are backed up to Essential Software's servers so they can be restored on another device, and your Pro purchase (if any) and any ad view-credit balance are linked to your account so they carry over too. Signing out stops further syncing but does not delete the backup already stored — sign back in to pick it up again. You can delete your account at any time by tapping the account icon and choosing Delete account under Show more. Doing so signs you out and schedules everything stored with it (synced notes, published pages, running ads, and any unspent ad view-credit balance) for permanent removal after 30 days. Signing back in with the same Google account during that window cancels the deletion and restores full access.

Publishing a page

Publishing is optional — it only happens when you tap Publish. Your page's content and the address you choose are sent to Essential Software and stored so the page can be served at a public link. Anyone with that link can view the page. Essential Software also gives you a private token for that page. It's stored on your device, not kept as-is on Essential Software's side — only a scrambled version of it is kept there, just enough to confirm it matches when you send it back to update or unpublish. Updating a published page sends the new content the same way. Unpublishing takes it down. A copy may be kept for up to 30 days afterward in case of an abuse report or takedown request, then deleted.

Publishing as an ad

From the Publish sheet's "Publish as Ad" tab, you can additionally register an already-published page to run as an ad, shown to other people using this app as a starting template when they tap Create — not only to people who have the page's link, which is how a regular published page works. Running an ad requires signing in. Buying views uses Google Play Billing; Essential Software receives the purchased product and confirmation of the purchase (not your payment details, which Google handles directly) and credits the corresponding number of views to your account. Essential Software also stores how many views an ad has used and its current status (running, used up, or taken down). To also report how many unique viewers an ad has reached, alongside its total view count, Essential Software stores an anonymous identifier generated and kept on each device — sent whenever a view is counted, whether or not the viewer is signed in. It isn’t linked to a Google account, email address, or any other identifying information, and exists only to tell whether a repeat view of a given ad came from a device already counted toward that ad; see “Analytics” below. Unpublishing an ad removes it from Create immediately and forfeits any views it had left — that balance is not restored to your account. The underlying published page and its normal link are unaffected by unpublishing an ad; taking the page itself down is still done separately from the Publish to Web tab. See "External images & embeds" below for how images, video, audio, and social-post embeds inside an ad are fetched — ads are additionally restricted to images from Wikipedia or Wikimedia Commons, and to video, audio, and social-post embeds added through the editor's own tools (YouTube, Instagram, or Spotify).

Reporting a published page

Anyone can report a published page from its public link. Reporting checks the reporter's IP address for about a minute, just to stop spam, then discards it — it's never stored as part of the report itself. Essential Software keeps only the reason and details submitted. Essential Software keeps every report on file so it can be reviewed. Reports of child sexual abuse material are specifically preserved, not deleted, because that material must be kept and passed to the proper authority.

This applies the same way to pages currently running as ads — an ad and its published page are the exact same thing at the exact same web address, so there's only one way to report either: go to that page's address and use the report link there. There's no separate process for ads.

Right now, the app doesn't show you that address while an ad appears as a starting point on the Create screen. To find it: without adding anything new to it, save the ad and open the Publish sheet for that note — it will automatically fill in the ad's own web address for you. Open that address in a browser and you'll see the report link.

External images & embeds

Images embedded in a page via URL are fetched directly from their source when the page is built. YouTube, Instagram, and Spotify embeds load directly from those services. Essential Software has no involvement with these third-party hosts. A page published as an ad is additionally restricted to images hotlinked from Wikipedia or Wikimedia Commons, and cannot contain images uploaded from your device — this is checked automatically before an ad can go live or be updated.

Linked pages

This section covers links inside the app. Tapping a link in a page shows its address in a sheet with a copy option. The app does not open, load, or navigate to the linked page — nothing is fetched, and Essential Software has no visibility into what links a page contains. A published page works differently: it's a plain web page viewed in a browser, so links inside it are ordinary clickable links that open like any other link on the web.

Analytics

Essential Software does not collect analytics, telemetry, or crash reports from this app. The one exception is the anonymous per-device identifier described under “Publishing as an ad” above: it exists only to count an ad’s unique viewers, isn’t used to track app usage generally, and doesn’t apply anywhere outside that feature.

Consumer Terms

Effective 22 September 2026

Using Note Builder means you agree to these terms.

Responsible Use

You agree to use Note Builder for lawful purposes only. You may not use the app to create, store, or export content that is illegal, harmful, threatening, abusive, defamatory, or infringes on the rights of others. This applies with extra weight to anything you publish — see below.

Your Content

Pages you build are stored on your device. If you sign in with Google, they're also backed up to Essential Software's servers so you can restore them on another device. You are responsible for keeping your own backups if you don't sign in — without an account, Essential Software has no copy of your content and cannot recover it if it's lost.

Your Account

Signing in is optional and handled by Google. Keep your Google account secure — anyone with access to it can access your synced notes, Pro entitlement, and ad view credits through this app.

Published Content

A published page is stored on Essential Software's servers and can be viewed by anyone with the link. You're responsible for what you publish and for having the rights to it. Essential Software may remove a published page if it breaks these terms, gets a valid takedown request, or is reported and found to be abusive. Unpublish it yourself and its address frees up right away for reuse. If Essential Software removes it instead, for a takedown or abuse report, the address stays down for good and can't be reclaimed or republished.

Advertising (Publish as Ad)

You may register an already-published page to run as an ad, purchasing a set number of views through Google Play Billing. To be eligible, a page must: contain no added text or captions beyond blank lines; keep the required attribution notice present, unedited, and clearly visible at its original size; contain no more than two images; and use only images linked directly from Wikipedia or Wikimedia Commons — no images uploaded from your device. A page may also include video, audio, and social-post embeds added through the editor's own Add media and Add post tools — YouTube, Instagram, and Spotify are the eligible sources, limited to one embed per platform; embeds added any other way are not eligible. An ad remains subject to the Responsible Use section above, and in addition may not contain sexual or adult content, or use its images, embeds, attribution, or branding to impersonate a person, brand, or organization, or otherwise mislead viewers about who or what it represents. Essential Software checks eligibility automatically before an ad can be published or updated, and may refuse or take down an ad that no longer meets these rules, or that otherwise breaks these terms. Since an ad and its underlying page are the same thing, reporting one reports the other.

A running ad is shown to other people using this app as a starting template on their Create screen, not only to people who have its link. Essential Software does not guarantee that an ad will receive any particular number of impressions in a given time, that the ad service will be available without interruption, or any outcome from an ad being shown.

A view is counted once someone actually begins editing a note handed to them as your ad, not merely when it’s shown on their Create screen. This is the standard cost-per-mille (CPM) model most ad platforms use: each view is counted as a plain impression, and a repeat view from the same person or device still counts and is still deducted from your view balance — views are not limited to first-time viewers. Note Builder also shows a separate unique viewers figure alongside your ad’s view count, for information only. It’s derived from an anonymous identifier generated and stored on each device, used solely to tell whether a device has already been counted once for a given ad; it isn’t tied to a Google account or any other identity, and is sent whether or not you’re signed in. Because it identifies a device rather than a person, someone viewing from two devices is counted as two unique viewers, and reinstalling the app or clearing its storage resets that device as a new one going forward. The unique viewers figure does not affect your view balance or how views are deducted, which follows the CPM model described above regardless of how many unique viewers it corresponds to.

Purchased views are a consumable purchase through Google Play — refer to Google Play's own refund policy for anything related to the purchase transaction itself. Separately, if Essential Software fails to deliver a view-credit balance you paid for, or takes down an ad in error after it was approved, contact Essential Software and it will, at its discretion, credit or refund the affected views; this is independent of, and doesn't replace, Google Play's own refund process for the purchase itself. Unpublishing an ad stops it from being shown and forfeits any views it had left; those views are not restored to your account or transferable to another ad, and any unspent view-credit balance is forfeited the same way if your account is deleted. Taking down the ad does not affect the underlying published page, which stays live until you unpublish it separately.

Purchases & Eligibility

Buying view packages is handled entirely through Google Play Billing, and any age or account requirements for making a purchase are set and enforced by Google Play, not by Essential Software. By buying a view package, you confirm you're permitted under Google Play's own terms to make purchases on the account you're using.

Third-Party Content

Images, video, and audio you embed by URL are loaded directly from the source you provide. You are responsible for having the right to use any content you embed. Images used in an ad are restricted as described above, and the required attribution notice exists specifically because third-party trademarks, logos, and brand names may appear in an ad's content or images — you're still responsible for having the right to use whatever you include, and that notice does not grant any rights of its own.

Changes to These Terms

Essential Software may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the app after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

Contact

Editor Guide

A note is made of blocks. Each block is one small piece — a heading, a photo, a quote — that you can add, move, and style on its own.

Add a block

Tap a button in the bar at the top: Heading, Subheading, Text, Checklist, Quote, Code, Image, Media, Social post, Table, or Divider. Some types ask you to pick a font, color, or layout first.

Move or resize a block

  • On the right side of a block, tap and hold the six-dot icon, then drag to move it.
  • Drag the double-arrow icon to make the block wider or narrower.
  • Tap the X icon to delete the block.

Change a photo, media, or post

Tap the pencil icon on the block. You can paste a link or upload a file from your device.

Add a caption or description

Image, Media, and Social post blocks have a small text area just below them. That area is for a caption or description. When you add one of these blocks, a blinking cursor appears there — start typing. Tap the X beside it to delete it. The arrows icon next to the X moves it above or below the block.

Style a block

On the left side of a block:

  • Tap the paint-drop icon to change its background color.
  • Tap the curved-arrow icon to tilt it.

Change the page background

Tap the round drop icon in the bottom-left corner. This colors the whole page, not just one block.

Preview your note

Tap the round icon in the bottom-right corner to see the note as it will look when saved or published, with all the editing controls hidden. Tap it again to go back to editing.

Format text

Select any text to open the format bar. From there you can bold, italicize, underline, add a link, change the color or font, and more.

Save note
Backup & Restore

Save every note as a single file, or bring notes back in from a file you saved earlier.

Online Publishing

Publish this note as a live page anyone can open with a link. Choose an address below using letters, numbers, and dashes.
